properties.profile: Spokesperson of the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology. Quoted on 4 and 5 September 2025 on the deactivation of unregistered platforms and on X asking for registration documents.

entities.title: Hit Raj Pandey

properties.profile: Chief whip of CPN (Maoist Centre) in the 4 September 2025 Kathmandu Post report. He called the shutdown objectionable and warned it could throw the country into disarray.

evidence.note: Single report; the quote was given to reporters outside Parliament.

entities.title: Bhola Nath Dhungana

properties.profile: President of Digital Rights Nepal. Told AFP, as reproduced by Al Jazeera on 4 September 2025, that the sudden closure directly hits fundamental rights.

entities.title: Shaswot Lamichhane

properties.profile: Described by Green European Journal as an 18-year-old who messaged Hami Nepal on 7 September 2025 about logistics and became a moderator of the Youths Against Corruption Discord server.

evidence.note: Age and role come from one article. Server username omitted on purpose.

entities.title: Rakshya Bam

properties.profile: Named as one of the coordinators calling themselves Gen Z leaders on 8 September 2025 (NHRC report as reported by HimalPress) and listed by Onlinekhabar among people who later emerged as Gen Z leaders.

entities.title: Jasmine Ojha

properties.profile: Named in the NHRC report, as reported by HimalPress, among protest coordinators who argued with Sudan Gurung at Maitighar on the morning of 8 September 2025.

evidence.note: Single source.

entities.title: Asheem Man Singh Basnyat

properties.profile: Then managing director of Pathao. Onlinekhabar reports he posted on the afternoon of Saturday 6 September 2025 that he would go to Maitighar on 8 September, and an intelligence report listed him as a possible participant.

evidence.note: Both articles are from Onlinekhabar.

entities.title: Nimesh Shrestha

properties.profile: TikTok content creator named by Nepali Times as publicly backing Hami Nepal, and by Onlinekhabar among the prominent voices calling for the 8 September 2025 protest.

entities.title: Apilraj Bohora

properties.profile: Kathmandu Police spokesperson (SP) at the time. Said before the protest that forces were on high alert and violators would face action.

entities.title: Hutaraj Thapa

properties.profile: Chief of the National Investigation Department at the time. Says written reports on the planned protest were submitted; one dated 7 September 2025 was obtained by Onlinekhabar.

entities.title: Instagram

properties.description: Meta-owned platform. Named by the Kathmandu Post among the platforms that did not apply to register by the deadline and were blocked from 4 September 2025. Hami Nepal used its Instagram account to circulate protest information.

entities.title: WhatsApp

properties.description: Meta-owned messaging platform. Named among the platforms that did not apply to register and were blocked from 4 September 2025.

entities.title: LinkedIn

properties.description: Professional network. Named among the platforms that did not apply to register and were blocked from 4 September 2025.

entities.title: Pinterest

properties.description: Image-sharing platform. Named by the Guardian and Swarajya among the blocked platforms.

entities.title: Signal

properties.description: Messaging app. Named by the Guardian and Swarajya among the blocked platforms.

entities.title: Viber

properties.description: Messaging platform. Listed as registered with the ministry, so not blocked on 4 September 2025.

entities.title: Digital Rights Nepal

properties.description: Rights group whose president, Bhola Nath Dhungana, criticised the 4 September 2025 closure as a hit on fundamental rights.

evidence.note: Single source.

entities.title: National Investigation Department

properties.description: Nepal’s intelligence agency under the Prime Minister’s Office. Onlinekhabar reports it filed a six-point report on the Gen Z movement on 7 September 2025.

evidence.note: Single source.

entities.title: Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal

properties.description: Industry body that the NTA instructed to enforce the blocking, according to Swarajya.

evidence.note: Single source; Swarajya attributes the report to The Kathmandu Post.

entities.title: Kathmandu District Security Committee

properties.description: District committee that met on 7 September 2025 and concluded the overall security situation was normal, per Onlinekhabar.

evidence.note: Single source.

entities.title: Everest Hotel, New Baneshwar

properties.description: Hotel on the route from Maitighar to New Baneshwar where police set up barricades and warned against entering the restricted zone on 8 September 2025; it is also named in the curfew order boundary.

evidence.note: Single geocoder record.
Barricades at the hotel: Kathmandu Post. Boundary of the curfew order via Everest Hotel: Himalayan Times / HimalPress texts for the order.

entities.title: Pathao

properties.description: Ride-hailing and delivery company. Its then managing director, Asheem Man Singh Basnyat, said he would join the 8 September 2025 protest at Maitighar.

evidence.note: Both articles are from Onlinekhabar.

entities.title: Ministry warns platforms to register within one month

properties.description: Onlinekhabar reports the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology warned on 20 March 2025 that platforms would be blocked if they did not register within one month.

evidence.note: One article. Outcome of the warning not reported.

entities.title: Cabinet directs platforms to register within one week

properties.description: A Cabinet decision, dated 25 August 2025 by Onlinekhabar and Swarajya and 26 August by Radio Nepal, directed that all social media platforms operating in Nepal register within one week. Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung later cited the decision and a Supreme Court directive.

evidence.note: Date conflicts: 25 August (Onlinekhabar, Swarajya, and CPJ via another part) vs 26 August (Radio Nepal). Swarajya cites the Kathmandu Post, so it may not be independent.

entities.title: Ministry issues seven-day registration notice to platforms

properties.summary: The Ministry of Communication and Information Technology published a notice giving platforms seven days to register, naming Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, X and LinkedIn. It followed a Cabinet instruction of 25 August and a 2023 directive that requires platforms to register and set up a local presence.

evidence.note: The deadline is described as seven days from 28 August, expiring Wednesday 3 September (Kathmandu Post, HRW) or Thursday midnight (Himalayan Times). See claim on the deadline.

entities.title: Registration deadline expires with no major global platform registered

properties.summary: The seven-day window expired with none of Meta, Alphabet, X, Reddit or LinkedIn having applied. Five platforms (TikTok, Viber and three others, named differently across outlets) were listed; Telegram and one more were awaiting approval. The Kathmandu Post and Al Jazeera put the deadline on Wednesday 3 September; The Himalayan Times says it expired Thursday at midnight.

evidence.note: Day of expiry conflicts: Wednesday 3 September (Kathmandu Post, Al Jazeera, HRW, Global Voices) vs Thursday midnight (Himalayan Times). See claim on the deadline.

entities.title: Ministry directs NTA to block unregistered platforms

properties.description: After a meeting of the ministry, the NTA, telecom operators and internet service providers chaired by Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung, the ministry directed the NTA to block access to platforms that had not registered. Reported figures range from about two dozen to 27 platforms; 26 is the most common. Registered platforms stayed available. The block was later withdrawn (BBC says on Monday night 8 September).

evidence.note: Who took the decision is disputed: ministry meeting (Kathmandu Post, Onlinekhabar 4 Sept) vs Cabinet meeting (Onlinekhabar one-year piece). Count and effective time also differ.
BBC: ban repealed Monday night; HRW: government has lifted the ban.

entities.title: Ministry directs NTA to block unregistered platforms

properties.summary: On Thursday 4 September 2025 a meeting at the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, chaired by Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung and attended by the NTA, telecom operators and ISPs, decided to block platforms that had not registered. Spokesperson Gajendra Kumar Thakur said unregistered platforms would be deactivated from that day and any platform completing registration would be reopened the same day. The government framed the move as enforcing a Supreme Court directive and curbing hate, rumours and cybercrime.

evidence.note: Decision-maker disputed: ministry meeting (Kathmandu Post, Onlinekhabar 4 Sept) vs Cabinet meeting (Onlinekhabar one-year piece).

entities.title: NTA instructs internet service providers to block platforms

properties.description: The NTA instructed mobile and internet service providers to block the listed platforms and, per Swarajya, told the Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal to enforce it through a technical committee. Swarajya expected restrictions to begin from Friday evening.

evidence.note: Start of restrictions conflicts: midnight Thursday (Kathmandu Post, Guardian) vs Friday evening (Swarajya) vs "since Friday" (BBC).
Block withdrawn after 8 September.

entities.title: X asks ministry for registration documents

properties.description: On Friday 5 September 2025 X emailed the ministry asking which documents it needed to register; the ministry replied by email, per spokesperson Gajendra Thakur. Swarajya separately reports the ministry confirmed Meta had emailed inquiries about documentation requirements.

evidence.note: X request: Onlinekhabar only. Meta inquiry: Swarajya only, date not given.

entities.title: Oli speech: nation’s independence greater than jobs of a handful

properties.description: In a speech on Sunday 7 September 2025, before the protest, Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli said he would not tolerate the nation being undermined and asked how it could be acceptable to defy the law and the constitution. Al Jazeera separately quotes him, undated, saying young people cannot think independently.

evidence.note: The 7 September speech is from the Guardian only. The Al Jazeera remark is undated ("ahead of the protest") and may be a different statement.

entities.title: Early Nepal-focused "nepo baby" video posted on TikTok

properties.summary: Onlinekhabar says one of the earliest nepo baby videos about Nepali politicians’ children was posted on TikTok on 2 September 2025 and drew over 350,000 views. The account holder is not identified. Three more videos followed on 6 September. The trend had come from Indonesia and the Philippines.

evidence.note: One article; account identity unknown, handle omitted.

entities.title: Political and rights-group reactions to the block

properties.summary: Critics included CPN (Maoist Centre) chief whip Hit Raj Pandey, Nepali Congress general secretary Gagan Thapa (4 September), Digital Rights Nepal, CPJ, Amnesty International and, on 8 September, the UN human rights office. The Nepali Congress was divided: its Central Working Committee had opposed the closure, party president Sher Bahadur Deuba said on 6 September the government only wanted registration, and on 8 September Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma urged him to press for reopening.

evidence.note: Each statement has its own source; see references.

entities.title: Gen Z march called for 8 September

properties.summary: From 6 September 2025 TikTok, Reddit and Discord filled with videos and posters announcing a protest on 8 September; AI-generated posters gave "Parliament Building" as the place. Hami Nepal’s founder announced the protest on Saturday, per India Today, while Onlinekhabar found no identifiable central organiser and Discord users picked Monday over Saturday. Maitighar was promoted as the gathering point because Parliament at New Baneshwar was a prohibited area. Demands: reopen social media, end corruption and nepotism. Organisers said it would be peaceful and non-political.

evidence.note: Who called it is disputed (see claim). The 6 September start of public calls is stated by Onlinekhabar (two articles) and India Today.

entities.title: Discord server "Youths Against Corruption" opens

properties.summary: At 9:35 pm on 7 September 2025 the first message appeared on a new Discord server called Youths Against Corruption, set up after Shaswot Lamichhane messaged Hami Nepal that morning. Within hours it carried protest guidelines (wear school uniform, document everything), a duty list, a protest website and banners with QR codes. Hami Nepal posted at 11:48 pm that it was not there to lead. A second server, Yuva Hub, was active from 7 September and Hami Nepal was admin of the first (commission report via Onlinekhabar).

evidence.note: Hour-level times come from Green European Journal only. India Today (8 Sept) already refers to Youths Against Corruption groups on Instagram and Discord created by Hami Nepal; the timing of its creation is not fully consistent across sources.

entities.title: Journalists protest the social media ban in Kathmandu

properties.summary: On Sunday 7 September 2025 dozens of journalists gathered in Kathmandu with signs such as "no shutdown of social networks" and "freedom of expression is our right".

evidence.note: heise gives no day, only "dozens of journalists chanted" in the capital; its page is dated 8 September.

entities.title: National Investigation Department report on planned Gen Z protest

properties.description: A six-point NID report dated 7 September 2025, obtained by Onlinekhabar, said activists and groups were preparing demonstrations against the ban in Kathmandu Valley and other districts, that a group had asked the district administration for security arrangements, and that Balen Shah had voiced support. It named possible participants. Its text says the march would start "from 8 a.m. on September 7", which is probably a slip for 8 September.

evidence.note: Only Onlinekhabar has seen the report. The date inside the report conflicts with the 8 September march date given everywhere else.

entities.title: Kathmandu District Security Committee meets, finds situation normal

properties.description: The committee met on 7 September 2025 and concluded the overall security situation was normal, calling for stronger coordination. The Karki Commission found no written Central Security Committee decision on a protest strategy for 5 to 10 September.

evidence.note: One article citing the commission report.

entities.title: Security forces prepare for Gen Z protest

properties.summary: On 7 September 2025 police deployed 3,441 personnel in Kathmandu Valley, then 505 more, with a command post under the chief district officer. Kathmandu Police spokesperson Apilraj Bohora said forces were on high alert after receiving videos calling for a peaceful protest but showing Parliament and Singha Durbar burning, and that violators would face action. Estimates of expected turnout differed widely between agencies.

evidence.note: Both articles are from Onlinekhabar. Deployment totals also differ (3,441 + 505 vs 4,396 per another official).

entities.title: Permission for the Maitighar protest sought from the district administration

properties.description: Sources disagree on who obtained or sought permission. Al Jazeera and India Today say the district administration or local media said Hami Nepal had secured approval. Onlinekhabar says two individuals went to the Kathmandu District Administration Office on 7 September. The NID report says a Gen Z group asked for security arrangements. The NHRC report (via HimalPress) says the rally began within boundaries permitted by the chief district officer.

evidence.note: Three different requesters named. See claim.

entities.title: Critics say the block was meant to stifle the anti-corruption campaign

properties.statement: Critics say the block was an attempt to stifle the online anti-corruption and anti-nepotism campaign. The government denies this and describes it as regulation.
properties.verification_note: BBC and Nepali Times report the critics’ view. Timing cuts against it: the Cabinet instruction (25 August) and the notice (28 August) predate the spread of nepo-kid content (first Nepal-focused TikTok video 2 September, Onlinekhabar). The government says it is enforcing a court directive and bringing platforms under Nepali law. No source shows the government’s intent either way.

evidence.note: BBC and Nepali Times report the critics’ view. Timing cuts against it: the Cabinet instruction (25 August) and the notice (28 August) predate the spread of nepo-kid content (first Nepal-focused TikTok video 2 September, Onlinekhabar). The government says it is enforcing a court directive and bringing platforms under Nepali law. No source shows the government’s intent either way.

entities.title: Government says the block enforces a Supreme Court directive

properties.statement: The government says the block follows a Supreme Court directive to list and monitor online platforms. Critics, including a Nepali Congress general secretary, say the court asked for legal mechanisms, not a shutdown by directive.
properties.verification_note: The directive text was not retrieved. Kathmandu Post and Himalayan Times report the government link; Gagan Thapa and an Onlinekhabar opinion piece dispute that the order authorises a block without a parliamentary law.

evidence.note: The directive text was not retrieved. Kathmandu Post and Himalayan Times report the government link; Gagan Thapa and an Onlinekhabar opinion piece dispute that the order authorises a block without a parliamentary law.

entities.title: Critics say the block violates freedom of expression

properties.statement: Rights groups, a Nepali Congress general secretary and commentators say the block breaches freedom of expression and the right to information. The government says it is not banning social media.
properties.verification_note: Positions are attributed; no court has ruled on the block in the retrieved sources. Government position in BBC and AP.

evidence.note: Positions are attributed; no court has ruled on the block in the retrieved sources. Government position in BBC and AP.

entities.title: Officials say this is registration, not a ban

properties.statement: Officials, including Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba on 6 September, say the government is not closing social media but requiring registration. Critics and several outlets call it a blanket ban.
properties.verification_note: Characterisation conflict: BBC, Kantipur and Setopati report the government view; Kathmandu Post and the Guardian describe a ban or blanket ban.

evidence.note: Characterisation conflict: BBC, Kantipur and Setopati report the government view; Kathmandu Post and the Guardian describe a ban or blanket ban.

entities.title: 26 platforms were blocked

properties.statement: Twenty-six platforms were blocked. Other counts reported are "about two dozen" (AP) and 27 (India Today). The Kathmandu Post names the seven exceptions but gives no total.
properties.verification_note: 26 appears in Guardian, BBC, Al Jazeera, HRW, Global Voices and Onlinekhabar. India Today says 27 "unregistered" sites; AP says "about two dozen". No retrieved source lists all platforms; the full list was not published in the sources found.

evidence.note: 26 appears in Guardian, BBC, Al Jazeera, HRW, Global Voices and Onlinekhabar. India Today says 27 "unregistered" sites; AP says "about two dozen". No retrieved source lists all platforms; the full list was not published in the sources found.

entities.title: Names of the five registered platforms differ

properties.statement: Five platforms had registered by the deadline: TikTok, Viber and three others. Outlets name the others as Witk, Nimbuzz and Popo Live (Kathmandu Post); Nimbuzz, WeTalk and Poppo Live (Himalayan Times); Nimbuzz, WeTalk and Opolite (Onlinekhabar). Telegram and a second platform ("Global Diary" or "GlobalLink") were in process.
properties.verification_note: Spelling or transliteration differences are likely (Witk/WeTalk, Popo Live/Poppo Live/Opolite, Global Diary/GlobalLink); the ministry notice was not retrieved to settle them.

evidence.note: Spelling or transliteration differences are likely (Witk/WeTalk, Popo Live/Poppo Live/Opolite, Global Diary/GlobalLink); the ministry notice was not retrieved to settle them.

entities.title: Registration deadline expired Wednesday night, 3 September

properties.statement: The seven-day registration window ended on Wednesday 3 September 2025. The Himalayan Times says it expired on Thursday at midnight, and Radio Nepal's notice report gives 4 September. Counting seven days from 28 August gives 4 September.
properties.verification_note: Four outlets give 3 September (Wednesday); Himalayan Times gives Thursday at midnight; Radio Nepal gives 4 September. The notice itself was not retrieved.

evidence.note: Four outlets give 3 September (Wednesday); Himalayan Times gives Thursday at midnight; Radio Nepal gives 4 September. The notice itself was not retrieved.

entities.title: Block took effect at midnight on Thursday 4 September

properties.statement: The block took effect at midnight on Thursday 4 September 2025. Other accounts: from 4 September "today" (ministry), Friday evening (Swarajya), difficulty from Friday (BBC); AFP found platforms reachable on Thursday.
properties.verification_note: Different reporters describe the order, the technical rollout and user experience, which may explain part of the gap. ISPs rolled out the block gradually (Onlinekhabar: "gradually blocked").

evidence.note: Different reporters describe the order, the technical rollout and user experience, which may explain part of the gap. ISPs rolled out the block gradually (Onlinekhabar: "gradually blocked").

entities.title: Cabinet, not the ministry, decided the 4 September block

properties.statement: Onlinekhabar’s one-year piece says a Cabinet meeting on 4 September decided to shut the platforms. Kathmandu Post and Onlinekhabar on 4 September say a ministry meeting decided, after a 25 August Cabinet instruction to register.
properties.verification_note: The two Onlinekhabar articles are a year apart. No Cabinet record for 4 September was found in the retrieved sources.

evidence.note: The two Onlinekhabar articles are a year apart. No Cabinet record for 4 September was found in the retrieved sources.

entities.title: Cabinet decision on platform registration dated 25 August

properties.statement: The Cabinet decision requiring platforms to register within one week was taken on 25 August 2025 (Onlinekhabar, Swarajya). Radio Nepal dates the Council of Ministers decision to 26 August.
properties.verification_note: One-day difference between outlets; the decision text was not retrieved. Swarajya cites the Kathmandu Post and the minister, so it may share an origin with Onlinekhabar.

evidence.note: One-day difference between outlets; the decision text was not retrieved. Swarajya cites the Kathmandu Post and the minister, so it may share an origin with Onlinekhabar.

entities.title: Discord was among the blocked platforms

properties.statement: Discord was on the list of blocked platforms, so organisers used a blocked service. The Kathmandu Post and the Guardian lists do not mention it.
properties.verification_note: Stated by heise, Swarajya, Green European Journal and Onlinekhabar. The Kathmandu Post list names only seven platforms as registered or pending. No outlet says Discord was left unblocked. Discord stayed usable through VPNs, per Green European Journal.

evidence.note: Stated by heise, Swarajya, Green European Journal and Onlinekhabar. The Kathmandu Post list names only seven platforms as registered or pending. No outlet says Discord was left unblocked. Discord stayed usable through VPNs, per Green European Journal.

entities.title: Hami Nepal organised the 8 September protest

properties.statement: Al Jazeera, India Today and Nepali Times describe Hami Nepal as an organiser or key coordinator. BBC, Onlinekhabar and Gurung himself say there was no single organiser or that he did not start the movement.
properties.verification_note: Onlinekhabar found that several people later seen as Gen Z leaders did not know who called the protest. Hami Nepal’s own 7 September post says it was only there to guide and keep people safe. The logistics role (tents, ambulances, sound) is not disputed in the NHRC report.

evidence.note: Onlinekhabar found that several people later seen as Gen Z leaders did not know who called the protest. Hami Nepal’s own 7 September post says it was only there to guide and keep people safe. The logistics role (tents, ambulances, sound) is not disputed in the NHRC report.

entities.title: Sudan Gurung took leadership of the crowd at Everest Hotel around noon

properties.statement: The NHRC investigation report, as reported by HimalPress, says Sudan Gurung of Hami Nepal took leadership of the crowd in front of Everest Hotel at about 12 pm on 8 September, after which protesters broke through barricades. It also says coordinators including Rakshya Bam and Jasmine Ojha argued with him at Maitighar around 9 am and asked him to withdraw.
properties.verification_note: Single report of the NHRC findings; the report itself was not retrieved. Hami Nepal posted on 7 September that it was not there to lead, and Gurung later said he was not the leader. Report date not shown on the page.

evidence.note: Single report of the NHRC findings; the report itself was not retrieved. Hami Nepal posted on 7 September that it was not there to lead, and Gurung later said he was not the leader. Report date not shown on the page.

entities.title: Hami Nepal obtained the district administration’s permission

properties.statement: Al Jazeera and India Today say Hami Nepal had obtained approval from the Kathmandu district administration. Onlinekhabar says two individuals went to the office on 7 September to seek permission, and the NID report says a Gen Z group asked for security arrangements.
properties.verification_note: Three different requesters are named. The district administration’s own record was not retrieved.

evidence.note: Three different requesters are named. The district administration’s own record was not retrieved.

entities.title: Expected turnout was about 8,000

properties.statement: The Valley Operations Division assessed around 8,000 protesters could attend. Others gave 6,000 to 7,000 (Oli), 3,500 to 5,000 (NID chief) and 3,000 to 5,000 (Kathmandu SSP). An NHRC-reported figure says the rally began with 3,000 to 3,200 and swelled to 20,000 to 25,000.
properties.verification_note: All pre-protest estimates come from testimony to the Karki Commission as reported by Onlinekhabar. Deployment figures also differ: 3,441 plus 505 police vs 4,396.

evidence.note: All pre-protest estimates come from testimony to the Karki Commission as reported by Onlinekhabar. Deployment figures also differ: 3,441 plus 505 police vs 4,396.

entities.title: Protests began on 1 September at Tribhuvan University

properties.statement: A timeline on RealShePower says student protests began at Tribhuvan University on 1 September 2025 under a "Youth Against Corruption" collective and that police used tear gas. No other retrieved source reports it.
properties.verification_note: Not corroborated by any other source retrieved. Onlinekhabar says there was no public discussion of a protest date until 6 September. Nepali Times traces the #youthsagainstcorruption campaign to Hami Nepal and the 8 September rally. The same article contains other claims that conflict with mainstream reporting (see related claims), so treat it as unreliable.

evidence.note: Not corroborated by any other source retrieved. Onlinekhabar says there was no public discussion of a protest date until 6 September. Nepali Times traces the #youthsagainstcorruption campaign to Hami Nepal and the 8 September rally. The same article contains other claims that conflict with mainstream reporting (see related claims), so treat it as unreliable.

entities.title: Curfews and a protester death before 8 September

properties.statement: RealShePower says curfews were imposed in Kathmandu Valley by 6 September and that a 19-year-old student was shot dead near Singha Durbar on 7 September. Other sources put the first deaths on 8 September.
properties.verification_note: The Kathmandu District Security Committee found the situation normal on 7 September; HRW, Kathmandu Post and others date the killings to 8 September. No other source reports a death on 7 September.

evidence.note: The Kathmandu District Security Committee found the situation normal on 7 September; HRW, Kathmandu Post and others date the killings to 8 September. No other source reports a death on 7 September.

entities.title: Partial shutdown of Facebook, X and TikTok announced 5 September

properties.statement: RealShePower says the government announced on 5 September a partial shutdown of platforms including Facebook, X and TikTok, effective 7 September. Mainstream sources say the order was on 4 September and TikTok was exempt.
properties.verification_note: Contradicted by AP, Guardian and Kathmandu Post (order on 4 September, TikTok registered and not blocked).

evidence.note: Contradicted by AP, Guardian and Kathmandu Post (order on 4 September, TikTok registered and not blocked).

entities.title: Curfew imposed on Sunday afternoon

properties.statement: Radio Nepal’s English report, dated 8 September, says a curfew was imposed in parts of Baneshwor on Sunday afternoon. Every other source dates the order to Monday 8 September.
properties.verification_note: Almost certainly a wrong weekday in the Radio Nepal text, since its own dateline is 8 September (a Monday). Recorded as a source error.

evidence.note: Almost certainly a wrong weekday in the Radio Nepal text, since its own dateline is 8 September (a Monday). Recorded as a source error.

properties.profile: On 8 September 2025, with Gagan Thapa, urged Nepali Congress president Sher Bahadur Deuba to listen to the Gen Z movement and reopen social media.

evidence.note: Single source.

properties.description: Kathmandu Post and Himalayan Times add that Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, X and LinkedIn were the platforms named in the public notice (12 Bhadra 2082), which the Kathmandu Post ties to the 2023 Directives for Managing the Use of Social Networks. Sources name that instrument differently and give the closing day as Wednesday 3 September, Thursday midnight, or 4 September.

evidence.note: Closing day conflicts across sources; see claim on the deadline.

properties.summary: Reports differ on when the block began: midnight on Thursday 4 September (Kathmandu Post, Guardian), "from today" (ministry spokesperson and minister), Friday evening (Swarajya), or noticed from Friday (BBC). AFP saw the platforms still reachable on Thursday. TikTok, which had registered, stayed available.

evidence.note: Start time conflicts across outlets. See claim on the start time.

properties.summary: Onlinekhabar traces the first Nepal-focused nepo-baby TikTok video to 2 September 2025, says the Indonesian and Philippine trend appeared on Nepali social media in the last week of August, and says content spread across countless accounts after 4 September. After the block TikTok, which stayed available, became the main channel and content moved to Instagram.

evidence.note: Timing relative to the ban is disputed (see claims by the background topic).

properties.description: Non-profit set up after the 2015 earthquake, formally registered in 2020, led by Sudan Gurung. In September 2025 reporting it used Instagram and Discord to circulate protest information and was the admin of the Youths Against Corruption Discord server.
